record.title: Microduck head-pitch output bracket — 'neck_pitch' in Pollen's MJCF: 35 x 18 x 27.7 mm U-bracket, XL330 horn pattern on both side plates + Ø16 boss yaw-output face on top, joining the head-pitch servo to the head-yaw servo
record.why: cad/part.py builds one valid solid (bin/cad part:microduck-neck-pitch-bracket, 2026-09-02) and ce-cad/bin/cad-refcheck grades it against Pollen's own published mesh reference/pollen-microduck-rl/assets/neck_pitch.stl: p95 surface distance 0.007 mm ref->ours / 0.007 mm ours->ref, bbox delta 0.00 mm per axis, volume ratio 1.0000, 21/21 reference holes and bosses matched, 0 unmatched (out/refcheck/microduck-neck-pitch-bracket/r1, evidence/refcheck/2026-09-01T19-38-41Z).
record.origin_why: modelled by hand in cecad from measurements taken off Pollen Robotics' decimated visual mesh (CC BY-SA-NC sim asset) with cecad.meshslice cut-plane probes (out/measure/neckgrp/np_slices_*.png) and cecad.meshfeatures; nobody has Pollen's CAD and no physical part has been measured. Admitted through the TRIAD.md door: evidence/ledger.jsonl + computed trust.json.
record.source_reference: reference/pollen-microduck-rl/assets/neck_pitch.stl (Pollen microduck RL assets, exported by onshape-to-robot)
record.why_this_folder_exists: The one bracket between the Microduck's head-pitch and head-yaw joints: its two R9-ended side plates take the head-pitch XL330's horn and idler between the neck plates, its Ø16-bossed top face is the head-yaw output that yaw_roll_motion's bearing and the yaw servo's horn ride on, and its underside is a Ø27.6 countersink-shaped clearance about the pitch axis so it can swing. Nothing on the shelf joins two XL330 axes at 90 deg 15.7 mm apart.
